---

## Work

Issue #460 (sub-issue of #441, §5): make the aggregation dispatch **fail-closed** and **one comment per completion**.

Repo `yuma-seno/atomaton`, workdir `/home/runner/work/atomaton/atomaton`, branch `atomaton/issue-460` (cut from `atomaton/issue-441`, the PR base — **not** `main`). Role `engineer`; this run was started by `atomaton`, then re-invoked by the machinery after a CI failure.

**PR #463 is open and pushed**: https://github.com/yuma-seno/atomaton/pull/463. Two commits:
- `9f5b250` Make the aggregation dispatch fail-closed on its own evidence
- `78ab045` Fix the e2e aggregation fixture for one-comment dispatch

## Decided (and why)

- **One comment per completion.** The gate already posts an `atomaton:aggregated` marker; the dispatch posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. `markerCommentId: markerId` is now passed, deleting the second POST. The marker body must carry `DISPATCH_TAG`, because `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only on a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch` — otherwise it posts a separate claim (two new comments again). Empty agent ⇒ tag omitted.
- **Fail-closed rule in `refuseOutstandingRequest`**: no marker + no ask of its own ⇒ `unconfirmed` (nothing dispatched, notice posted); no marker + caller-supplied ask (the runner hand-off's result comment) ⇒ still dispatched with the ordering check skipped. Answers-request dispatches post no marker and are untouched.
- **No double DELETE.** `dispatchRunner`'s own `removeMarker` deletes a caller-supplied marker on `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`. So `aggregation.ts` must NOT `takeBackMarker` for those two — a second DELETE answers 404 and logs "the marker could not be removed, so nothing will retry", the opposite of the truth. `unconfirmed` maps to `dispatch-failed` with no DELETE. Only `failed` (GitHub rejected the dispatch) reaches `takeBackMarker`.
- **Regression caught and repaired**: `refused-closed` deliberately keeps the marker, but once it carries `atomaton:dispatch` a closed parent holds a phantom ask forever — `runInFlight` reads that as "a run is coming", and `prune_atomaton_data` never prunes. That branch now PATCHes the tag off (`takeBackDispatchTag`), keeping the `atomaton:aggregated` line.
- `dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`'s wording widened to cover both "could not be posted" and "posted but never visible".

## Done (all measured)

**Source** — `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.ts` (new `refuseUnconfirmed(d, why)` helper shared by both unconfirmed paths; the markerless branch; doc updates incl. `markerCommentId`'s third caller), `src/app/aggregation.ts` (`DISPATCH_TAG` import, hoisted `agent`, `markerLines`, `markerCommentId`, `takeBackDispatchTag`, outcome mapping rewritten), `src/domain/work/closed-target.ts` (notice doc + body), `src/entrypoints/machinery/dispatch_agent.ts` (unconfirmed `::error::` wording), `src/entrypoints/tools/lib/dispatch_sub_agent.ts` (new `unconfirmed` throw instead of "see the workflow log").

**Tests** — `src/app/aggregation.test.ts` (`runGateDetailed` added; `MARKER_ID = 777`; `thread()` appends a neutral entry with that id; `PARKED` = `<!-- atomaton:ended=waiting answers=0 run=0 -->` in `PARENT_AGENT`; `DISPATCH_MARKER` const deleted; 3 new tests: one-comment/both-tags/`ask=777`, unconfirmed-not-sent-with-exactly-one-DELETE, closed-parent-loses-the-tag), `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.test.ts` (`describe("the dispatch's own evidence")`, 2 tests), `src/entrypoints/machinery/dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts` (one POST rule → 556, three-comment thread, exactly-one-write assertion), `tests/e2e/request-close-issue-aggregation.e2e.test.ts` (fixture fixed + asserts one write, both tags, `ask=777`).

**Verification, all run locally and green:**
- `bun run typecheck` → 0
- `bun run src/entrypoints/machinery/scan_secrets.ts` → 0
- `bun run synth` → 0
- `bun run test` → **2197 pass, 0 fail**
- `ATOMA_BIN=/usr/local/bin/atoma bun test` (whole tree incl. e2e) → **2208 pass, 0 fail**
- `ATOMA_BIN=/usr/local/bin/atoma bun run test:e2e` → **11 pass, 0 fail**
- `ATOMA_BIN=/usr/local/bin/atoma bun run .github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/check_live_tools.ts` → exit 0
- `ATOMA_BIN=/usr/local/bin/atoma bash .github/atomaton/scripts/check-live-tools.sh` → exit 0, "5 server(s) started and answered"

**CI on `78ab045`**: `atomaton-tools` **success** (the job that failed before), `plan-*` success, `default-branch-checks` skipped, `pull-request-checks (verify)` was **still in_progress** at the last check.

## The CI failure that started this run (resolved)

Run 42253585871 / job 128014740034 `atomaton-tools` failed at `tests/e2e/request-close-issue-aggregation.e2e.test.ts:283` (`expect(...workflow run...).toBe(true)`), because the fixture never showed the marker's own id so the freshness probe stood down `unconfirmed`. Cause of my missing it: `bun run test` **excludes** `tests/e2e`; the documented way to run it is `bun run test:e2e` (prefixed by `pretest:e2e` = `bun run synth`). `atoma 0.4.5` is installed at `/usr/local/bin/atoma`, so e2e is runnable here — **run `bun run test:e2e` whenever e2e is touched.**

## Still open

1. `pull-request-checks (verify)` on `78ab045` had not finished. Re-check with `get_check_runs(ref="78ab045")`. Everything it runs already passes locally.
2. The PR body's "New tests" bullet for `dispatch.test.ts` got its path mangled (it reads a truncated form); the sent text was correct. Worth correcting if the body is edited anyway — the e2e gap and its fix are **not** yet recorded in the PR body or a PR comment, and should be.
3. Nothing is merged. #460 closes only after #441's branch carries the work and a person confirms on the parent.

## Must not

- Bump `version` in `package.json`, release, or edit `.github/**`, `dist/**`, `.github/atomaton-runtime/**`.
- Re-add the double DELETE in `aggregation.ts` for `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`.
- Break the answers-request path (`answersRequest` dispatches post no marker and must keep going out).
- Put atomaton issue numbers (`#NNN`) into `docs/`.
- Re-do the e2e fixture repair — it is committed and verified against the real binary.
- No tool-degradation report was encountered; nothing to file with `create_root_issue`.

## 済み済み(再実装しない)
- §1/§2 は core 側: yuma-seno/atoma v0.4.5(yuma-seno/atoma#17 / #18)。compaction の予算修正と `context_limit` ending 名。
- §3 は #455 マージ済み(post_result_comment の skip 反転 + failure-notice 共通化)。#454 で `context_limit` 語彙接続済み。
- v0.21.56 リリース & self-deploy 済み。

## 棚卸し(現行 head 884da10 = #457 マージ後の実測。この一次情報を起点にし、編集前に自分でも当該箇所を開いて確認すること)

1. `src/entrypoints/machinery/aggregate_sub_issues.ts:58` → `dispatchOrchestratorIfReady({repo, parent, closedNum, exclude, progress})` — `ask` も `markerCommentId` も渡していない。
2. `src/app/aggregation.ts:332-336` — 集約は**既に** `commentOnWithId` で `<!-- atomaton:aggregated=N -->` マーカーを投稿して `markerId` 変数に保持している。`null` のときは `:337-342` で fail-closed 済み(「a failed marker write stops the dispatch rather than racing on」)。dispatch 呼び出しは `:344-352` で markerId を渡していない。take-back は `:364` と `:386-391` で markerId を再利用。
3. `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.ts:678-684` — `markerCommentId` は**既に引数として存在**(`:173` 宣言、doc `:157-172`:「outstanding read から除外し、freshness probe に marker と同じ役目をさせる」)。caller が渡す先例: `src/adapters/actions/dispatch-targets.ts:154`/`:171`(`dispatchPostMergeAgent`)と `:240`/`:258`(`dispatchRejectedPrAgent`)。
4. **穴**: `postDispatchMarker`(`dispatch.ts:368`)の POST が非ゼロで終わると `undefined` を返し(`:383-386`)、`refuseOutstandingRequest` は `:447` の `if (markerId === undefined) return undefined;` で**dispatch を続行**する(コメント `:444-446` が根拠)。POST は成功したが可視化が遅れた場合は `:468-515` で fail-closed(再投稿 → `removeMarker()` → `"unconfirmed"`)。今回塞ぐのは前者だけ。
5. answers-request 経路は marker 無しで dispatch する設計(`:674-677`、`refuseSupersededAsk` `:577`)。ask は回答コメント自身。ここを壊さないこと。
6. freshness probe は `checkDispatchMarker`(`dispatch.ts:455`)で marker 上の dispatch タグ(`DISPATCH_TAG = stringTag("dispatch", …)`, `src/adapters/github/tags.ts:298`)を読む。採用したコメントにタグを書いておく必要があるかはこの実装で確認。
7. テスト: `src/app/aggregation.test.ts`(18 tests — 単一 dispatch、marker 書き込み冪等、marker 書き込み失敗で停止、失敗 dispatch で marker take-back)、`src/adapters/actions/dispatch.test.ts`(529 行。`unconfirmed` 経路は tested、**POST 非ゼロ失敗経路は無テスト**)、`dispatch_agent.test.ts` / `dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts` / `dispatch_post_merge.test.ts` / `dispatch_rejected.test.ts`。

## スコープ(設計は決済済み。議論の余地があるのは手段のみ)

1. `aggregation.ts:344` の dispatch 呼び出しに `markerCommentId: markerId` を渡す。自前シード POST(`postDispatchMarker`)はこの経路から消える。
2. 採用する集約マーカーが freshness probe が読める形、すなわち dispatch タグをそのコメントに carries するようにする(`dispatch-targets.ts` の directive-as-marker 先例に倣う。edit で追加でよいか、probe の読み方で決める)。
3. `dispatch.ts:447` の穴を塞ぐ: caller からの ask/marker も無く marker POST も失敗した場合、**dispatch を実行しない**(refusal として返す)。answers-request のように ask が caller 提供の経路は現行どおり dispatch できること。
4. 採用したマーカーに対する take-back(`:441` の DELETE が何を消すか)を推論してコメント/テストで固定する。DELETE なら集約マーカーの idempotency(「aggregated marker があれば再集約しない」)との関係(=失敗 dispatch を sweep/再集約が拾える、が正か)を明記。

## 受け入れ条件

- 集約による dispatch のたびにスレッドに新規投稿されるコメントは 1 件(集約マーカー)で、それが dispatch タグと ask を兼ねる。第 2 の marker コメントは投稿されない。
- marker を用意できない場合(集約マーカー投稿失敗は既に fail-closed、これに加えて dispatch 側の POST 失敗経路)、`workflow_dispatch` が飛ばない(gh 呼び出しの call log で確認)。
- answers-request 経路の既存テストが一切変わらず通る。
- `dispatch.test.ts` に「marker POST が非ゼロで失敗 → dispatch されない」テストが追加される。
- 上記の既存テスト群が全て通る。

## 制約

- 挙動の劣化禁止。既存契約テスト(stopped / limit 経路を含む)を壊さない。
- version bump とリリースはしない(人がまとめて行う)。
- `docs/` に自リポジトリ(atomaton)の issue 番号(#NNN)は書かない。
- core リポジトリ(yuma-seno/atoma)には触れない。
- workflow の yml は wac.ts から生成されるため、触る場合は `bun run synth`(生成物もコミット)。

## クローズ条件

この issue(#441)のブランチにマージされた PR の head で次が観察できること: (1) aggregation がマーカー id を渡すコード+「投稿は 1 件」を固定するテスト。(2) POST 失敗時に dispatch しないコード+それを固定するテスト。(3) answers 経路を含む既存 dispatch/aggregation テストの green 実行結果。エンジニアが PR に検証結果を残し、親(#441)側で統合確認のうえ閉じる。","total_comments":1,"parent":{"number":441,"title":"run 失敗時に ending が投稿されない経路がある（#12 のセッション上限死で観測）","state":"open"},"children":[],"pull_requests":[]}

Let me review the diff once more carefully, then commit and create the PR.

Let me double-check requirement 4: "採用したマーカーに対する take-back(`:441` の DELETE が何を消すか)を推論してコメント/テストで固定する。DELETE なら集約マーカーの idempotency(「aggregated marker があれば再集約しない」)との関係(=失敗 dispatch を sweep/再集約が拾える、が正か)を明記。"

I've done this in the aggregation.ts comments and the test asserts exactly one DELETE. But I should also verify the sweep/retry path — describeGateResult's promise about retry. Let me look at `needsAttention` and `describeGateResult` for `dispatch-failed`.

Also requirement: "集約マーカー投稿失敗は既に fail-closed" — covered.

Let me check describeGateResult wording for dispatch-failed to ensure it says retry and is accurate now that the unconfirmed path is also dispatch-failed.

The `describeGateResult` for `dispatch-failed` says "The aggregation marker was removed, so closing a sub-issue again retries it". That is still true for both `failed` and `unconfirmed` now. Good.

Let me double-check the wording: "the dispatch FAILED" — for unconfirmed it's more that it could not be confirmed. It's acceptable but let me review whether to distinguish. The issue asks for keeping behaviour. `dispatch-failed` is reported for both. I think adding a small distinction would be an improvement but `undetermined`-style. Let me keep it simple — the describe string is generic enough.

Now let's also double check the `describeGateResult` test "the two outcomes that take the marker back promise a retry" still holds. Yes.

Let me review the full diff of aggregation.ts one more time and then check the answers-request path tests all pass. Then commit.

Also I should double check: in `dispatchRunner`, when `markerCommentId` is provided and the dispatch is `unconfirmed`... the repost is skipped (ownMarker false), removeMarker deletes the caller's marker. Good.

And for `failed` (workflow dispatch rejected) with markerCommentId provided: `if (d.refusalEnding !== undefined)` — aggregation doesn't pass refusalEnding, so the marker stays and aggregation's takeBackMarker removes it. Good, exactly one DELETE. Confirmed by test.

For `refused-outstanding` with adopted marker: `removeMarker()` inside refuseOutstandingRequest deletes the adopted marker (the caller's comment). Then aggregation does not delete again. Good.

Now, one thing to verify: is there any other caller that passes `markerCommentId` and ALSO does its own delete on refused-outstanding? Let's check dispatch-targets.ts and dispatch_sub_agent, resume_subtree, atomaton.ts.

dispatchPostMergeAgent: no delete after; returns boolean. It only posts a comment if markerCommentId === null. Wait — it returns false if the marker post fails. And for refused-outstanding, removeMarker deletes the directive comment. That was already the behaviour before my change? Let's check: previously `refuseOutstandingRequest` with markerId defined did `removeMarker()` on outstanding. Yes, same. Good.

Now let me also double check `dispatch_agent.ts`: it passes `ask` from `--ask`. For marker dispatches (the runner's hand-off), `ask` IS provided (postResultCommentStep.outputs.comment_id). So `refuseOutstandingRequest` with markerId from postDispatchMarker failing → d.ask defined → returns undefined → dispatch proceeds with `ask = d.ask ?? markerId` = the caller's ask. Good — hand-offs keep working, as tested.

But wait: for the runner hand-off, if the marker POST fails AND the ask comment doesn't exist... it still goes out. That's the documented exception. Fine per the design decision.

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: is that a hole? The ask is the run's own result comment which the run claims. So the record exists. Fine.

For `resume_subtree.ts`: no ask passed. markerId undefined → unconfirmed → warning "could not resume". That's fail-closed, correct.

For `dispatch_sub_agent.ts` (launch_sub_agent): no ask. markerId undefined → unconfirmed → throws generic "could not dispatch... see the workflow log". Hmm, that message is misleading for unconfirmed. Let me improve that — a dedicated branch like refused-outstanding.

Let me look at it.

{"title": "Make the aggregation dispatch fail-closed on its own evidence", "reviewer": "reviewer", "body": "## What this changes

The aggregation gate already wrote an `atomaton:aggregated` marker before dispatching; the dispatch then posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. Two comments said one thing, and the second was the run's ask.

**1. One comment per completion.** `dispatchRunner` now receives the marker's id as its `markerCommentId`, so the marker the gate already wrote is both the idempotency claim and the ask the run claims. Its body carries `DISPATCH_TAG` as well as `AGGREGATED_TAG`, which is not cosmetic: `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only on a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch`, and posts a separate claim for any other. Without the tag, every aggregation would be two new comments again. The tag is omitted when the parent's thread names no agent — an empty `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader, and the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.

**2. The fail-closed hole.** `postDispatchMarker` returning `undefined` used to leave `refuseOutstandingRequest` returning early with the dispatch *continuing* — ordering check skipped, and a run with nothing on the thread to account for it: no marker for `wasLaunchedOn`, `mostRecentAgentOn` or the guard to read, and no ask for the runner to claim, so `claim_turn.ts` writes nothing and the run watch cannot tell it from a run that died. Now:

- no marker **and** no ask of its own → `unconfirmed`, nothing dispatched, notice posted;

## What this changes

Without the tag, every aggregation would be two new comments again. The tag is omitted when the parent's thread names no agent — an empty `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader, and the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.

**2. The fail-closed hole.** `postDispatchMarker` returning `undefined` used to leave `refuseOutstandingRequest` returning early with the dispatch *continuing* — ordering check skipped, and a run with nothing on the thread to account for it: no marker for `wasLaunchedOn`, `mostRecentAgentOn` or the guard to read, and no ask for the runner to claim, so `claim_turn.ts` writes nothing and the run watch cannot tell it from a run that died. - no marker **and** no ask of its own → `unconfirmed`, nothing dispatched, notice posted;

POST returns, deliberately untagged so the gate's own idempotency read does not

to the parent's thread, its body carrying both tags, and `ask=777` on the

{"baseRefName":"atomaton/issue-441","createdAt":"2026-11-06T16:33:49Z","headRefName":"atomaton/issue-460","number":463,"state":"OPEN","title":"Make the aggregation dispatch fail-closed on its own evidence","body":"/reviewer

Part of #460
## What this changes

The aggregation gate already wrote an `atomaton:aggregated` marker before dispatching; the dispatch then posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. Two comments said one thing, and the second was the run's ask.

**1. One comment per completion.** `dispatchRunner` now receives the marker's id as its `markerCommentId`, so the marker the gate already wrote is both the idempotency claim and the ask the run claims. Its body carries `DISPATCH_TAG` as well as `AGGREGATED_TAG`, which is not cosmetic: `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only on a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch`, and posts a separate claim for any other. Without the tag, every aggregation would be two new comments again. The tag is omitted when the parent's thread names no agent — an empty `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader, and the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.

**2. The fail-closed hole.** `postDispatchMarker` returning `undefined` used to leave `refuseOutstandingRequest` returning early with the dispatch *continuing* — ordering check skipped, and a run with nothing on the thread to account for it: no marker for `wasLaunchedOn`, `mostRecentAgentOn` or the guard to read, and no ask for the runner to claim, so `claim_turn.ts` writes nothing and the run watch cannot tell it from a run that died. Now:

- no marker **and** no ask of its own → `unconfirmed`, nothing dispatched, notice posted;
- no marker **but** a caller-supplied ask (the runner's hand-off, whose result comment is the record) → still dispatched, check skipped, exactly as before.

The answers-request path posts no marker by design and is untouched — all its tests pass unchanged.

**3. The take-back, reasoned rather than guessed.** Because the marker is now the comment `dispatchRunner` was handed, its own `removeMarker` deletes it on `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`. The gate therefore no longer deletes it a second time: a 404 there was logged as "the marker could not be removed, so nothing will retry", which is the opposite of what happened. Only `failed` (GitHub rejecting the dispatch, marker still standing) reaches `takeBackMarker` now.

**4. One regression I introduced and then repaired.** `refused-closed` deliberately keeps the marker. Once the marker carries `atomaton:dispatch`, a closed parent would hold a standing request forever — `runInFlight` reads that as a run working or coming, and `prune_atomaton_data` would never prune the node. That is the shape #449 was made of. That branch now PATCHes the tag off, keeping the idempotency claim (`"aggregated"` is the true half) and dropping the promise.

`dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`'s wording was widened: it now covers both "could not be posted" and "posted but never visible", instead of claiming GitHub hid the machinery's own marker.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Full `bun test` (after `bun run synth`, so `dist/` exists): **2202 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail**, 6671 expects, 176 files.
- New tests:
  - `src/app/aggregation.test.ts` — "an aggregation posts exactly one comment, and it is both the marker and the ask" (asserts exactly one `--method` write, both tags on it, `ask=777` on the dispatch); "a dispatch the thread cannot confirm is not sent, and the marker comes back" (no `workflow_dispatch`, exactly **one** DELETE of the marker); "a closed parent's marker keeps the aggregation claim and loses the dispatch tag".
  - `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.test.ts` — `describe("the dispatch's own evidence")`: marker POST fails + no ask → `unconfirmed`, no `workflow` call, notice posted; marker POST fails + caller's ask → `dispatched` with `ask=900`.
  - `src/entrypoints/machinery/dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts` — first test rewritten to one POST rule (`atomaton:aggregated` → 556) and asserts exactly one write carrying both tags.

## Not done, deliberately

- No version bump, no release, no `docs/` change (nothing there describes the aggregation comment's shape), no `.github/**` or `dist/**` edit. `dist/` is gitignored and was only rebuilt so the generated-workflow tests could run.

# Skill: project/conventions

# Repository conventions

This repository builds Atomaton, the delivery template. It is both the producer of
that template and an adopter of it, which creates rules that do not apply
anywhere else.

This file is not part of the template. Its source is `self/atomaton/skills/project/`,
and it is deliberately absent from `src/` so adopters never receive it.

## The four trees

| Tree | What it is | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/**` | Source of the deliverable | You |
| `dist/.github/**` | The deliverable adopters receive | The build |
| `self/**` | This repository's own files, the ones that are not the template's | You |
| `.github/**` | This repository's running configuration | The self-deploy job, from a release plus `self/` |

Two different activities live in this table, and which one you are doing decides
which rules apply:

- **improving the deliverable** — `src/**`. It affects every adopter, and it
  reaches this repository only after a release and a self-deploy.
- **improving this repository's own operation** — `self/**`. It affects nobody
  else, and it applies as soon as it merges.

The rest of this file does not separate them cleanly. That is a known gap, tracked
in the documentation restructure; until then, read each rule and ask which of the two it is about.

`src/content/**` is mirrored verbatim into `dist/.github/atomaton/` and from there
into an adopter's repository. **It may only contain content that holds for any
project using Atomaton.** No reference to this repository's build pipeline, no
mention of `dist/`, `bun run synth`, or `build-dist.ts`, and no incident history
or PR numbers. If a rule is about developing *this* repository, it belongs in
this file instead.

## Generated output is not tracked

Change `src/**` only. `dist/**` is gitignored, so there is nothing generated to
commit and nothing to keep in sync.

Run `bun run synth` freely to inspect what adopters would receive. It writes only
into the ignored `dist/`, so it cannot dirty your commit.

Adopters receive the deliverable from a release, not from a merge, so nothing you
merge needs to carry it.

**Never touch `version` in `package.json`.** The version is the release declaration:
merging an edit to it publishes to adopters, and that decision belongs to a person,
made on the pull request the **Atomaton Release** workflow opens — never inside a
work pull request. A version left alone is a merge that publishes nothing, which is
the normal case. A work pull request that arrives with a version change in it is a
merge-blocking defect: flag it, and have the edit taken back out before merge.

`.github/**` is a different matter — see below. It is tracked, and every file in it
comes from either the release or `self/`.

## main is protected; everything lands by pull request

`.github/atomaton/rulesets/main.json` is the source of truth for what may reach main:
direct pushes are refused, and a pull request cannot merge until the `check` job
passes. It is applied by hand from an account with admin, and taken as correctly
configured thereafter — nothing verifies it, because a check could only report and
never enforce: with no ruleset, `check` would not be a required context either.

Changing the rule is a pull request against the JSON, followed by one `gh api`
call from an account with admin (see CONTRIBUTING.md). CI cannot make that call —
`administration` is not a permission a workflow can hold.

`check_merge_readiness` reports against whatever the ruleset currently
requires, so it follows the file rather than holding a second opinion.

Nothing bypasses it. No workflow writes to main — the release job attaches the deliverable
to a release instead — and your merge satisfies the rules like anyone else's. Do
not propose a bypass actor: it would mean naming a GitHub App ID or a deploy key,
values that exist only after manual setup, so the JSON would stop describing the
whole configuration.

The workflows that run agents are generated from `src/workflows/` and shipped.
`self/workflows/` holds the two that are not: `atomaton-self-deploy.yml` and
`probe-dumpable.yml`.

## Adding a static file to the deliverable

A new non-code file under `src/content/` must also be added to `build-dist.ts`'s
verbatim-copy list, or it never reaches `dist/` at all.
`tests/contract/deployment-contract.test.ts` enforces this.

## `atoma validate` is on the CLI

The `atoma` binary is on the agent's PATH — the runner installs it at
`/usr/local/bin/atoma` — and it has a `validate` subcommand that checks an agent
definition against a tools file without starting a run:

```bash
atoma validate --agent-def .github/atomaton/agent-definitions/engineer.md \
               --tools-file /tmp/tools.yaml
```

It resolves every name in the definition's `mcp_servers` against the tools file,
checks the template's placeholders, and reports what it finds. `atomaton-validate-pr`
runs it on every pull request that touches an agent definition, so a definition
that names a server `tools.yaml` does not define is a red check rather than a run
that aborts before a single tool starts.

There is no MCP tool for it, and that is deliberate: it is a check a person or a
workflow runs, not something an agent needs mid-run. Use it from the shell when
you are changing a definition and want the same answer CI will give.

## `.github/` is an adoption, not a mirror

Nothing regenerates `.github/` automatically. It is this repository's deliberate
adoption of the deliverable, so it lags `src/` until someone applies a release.

**That lag is the point.** A change to `src/` must not reconfigure the live agents
the moment it merges. Two breakages reached the running system exactly that way.

### Applying a release

Dispatch **Atomaton Self Deploy** (`self/workflows/atomaton-self-deploy.yml`) from the
Actions tab. It opens a pull request and merges nothing. `.github/**` is in
`merge.governed_paths`, so a person reviews it.

What it does:

```bash
rm -rf .github            # so a file the release DELETED is gone, not orphaned
unzip release.zip         # the deliverable
cp -r self/. .github/     # this repository's own, at the same paths
```

`.github/` is therefore exactly those two sources, with nothing kept alive by
remembering to. Before `self/` existed this was a `cp -r` followed by
`git checkout -- .github/atomaton/config.yaml`, and a file the template had removed
stayed in the tree with no diff to notice it by.

It needs `SELF_DEPLOY_TOKEN`, a PAT with the `workflow` scope, because
`GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/**` — refused on identity, not by
path. No agent can reach that token: it is named in one file outside the
deliverable, and `atomaton-runner.yml` does not mention it.

### Changing something in `self/`

An overlay entry is a copy, not a build, so it needs no release. Change
`self/X` and `.github/X` **in the same pull request**, identically.

`tests/contract/self-overlay.test.ts` requires them byte-identical, in both
directions. Editing `.github/X` alone is worse than not editing it at all: the next
self-deploy overwrites it from `self/` and the change disappears without a diff.

A file added to `.github/` that is in no release and not in `self/` is not checked
for, because the next deploy removes it anyway and because `.github/**` is in

Part of #460
## What this changes

The aggregation gate already wrote an `atomaton:aggregated` marker before dispatching; the dispatch then posted a second `atomaton:dispatch` marker beside it. Two comments said one thing, and the second was the run's ask.

**1. One comment per completion.** `dispatchRunner` now receives the marker's id as its `markerCommentId`, so the marker the gate already wrote is both the idempotency claim and the ask the run claims. Its body carries `DISPATCH_TAG` as well as `AGGREGATED_TAG`, which is not cosmetic: `claim_turn.ts` appends its `atomaton:took` line **in place** only on a comment carrying `atomaton:dispatch`, and posts a separate claim for any other. Without the tag, every aggregation would be two new comments again. The tag is omitted when the parent's thread names no agent — an empty `atomaton:dispatch=` matches no reader, and the dispatch refuses an empty agent anyway.

**2. The fail-closed hole.** `postDispatchMarker` returning `undefined` used to leave `refuseOutstandingRequest` returning early with the dispatch *continuing* — ordering check skipped, and a run with nothing on the thread to account for it: no marker for `wasLaunchedOn`, `mostRecentAgentOn` or the guard to read, and no ask for the runner to claim, so `claim_turn.ts` writes nothing and the run watch cannot tell it from a run that died. Now:

- no marker **and** no ask of its own → `unconfirmed`, nothing dispatched, notice posted;
- no marker **but** a caller-supplied ask (the runner's hand-off, whose result comment is the record) → still dispatched, check skipped, exactly as before.

The answers-request path posts no marker by design and is untouched — all its tests pass unchanged.

**3. The take-back, reasoned rather than guessed.** Because the marker is now the comment `dispatchRunner` was handed, its own `removeMarker` deletes it on `refused-outstanding` / `unconfirmed`. The gate therefore no longer deletes it a second time: a 404 there was logged as "the marker could not be removed, so nothing will retry", which is the opposite of what happened. Only `failed` (GitHub rejecting the dispatch, marker still standing) reaches `takeBackMarker` now.

**4. One regression I introduced and then repaired.** `refused-closed` deliberately keeps the marker. Once the marker carries `atomaton:dispatch`, a closed parent would hold a standing request forever — `runInFlight` reads that as a run working or coming, and `prune_atomaton_data` would never prune the node. That is the shape #449 was made of. That branch now PATCHes the tag off, keeping the idempotency claim (`"aggregated"` is the true half) and dropping the promise.

`dispatchUnconfirmedNotice`'s wording was widened: it now covers both "could not be posted" and "posted but never visible", instead of claiming GitHub hid the machinery's own marker.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Full `bun test` (after `bun run synth`, so `dist/` exists): **2202 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail**, 6671 expects, 176 files.
- New tests:

  - `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.test.ts` — `describe("the dispatch's own evidence")`: marker POST fails + no ask → `unconfirmed`, no `workflow` call, notice posted; marker POST fails + caller's ask → `dispatched` with `ask=900`.
  - `src/entrypoints/machinery/dispatch_if_siblings_done.test.ts` — first test rewritten to one POST rule (`atomaton:aggregated` → 556) and asserts exactly one write carrying both tags.

## Not done, deliberately

- No version bump, no release, no `docs/` change (nothing there describes the aggregation comment's shape), no `.github/**` or `dist/**` edit. `dist/` is gitignored and was only rebuilt so the generated-workflow tests could run.
